Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Title

Project: an event flyer from brief to print

Put it together: a one-page flyer for a real Club event, designed from a brief and checked before printing.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Work from a client brief
  • Apply hierarchy, grid, colour and images together
  • Check a design with a proof checklist
Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Idea 1

Understand it

A brief says who it is for, what it must say, the size, and the deadline. Designers start with thumbnails — tiny quick sketches — before the computer. If you ask an AI tool for headline ideas, treat them as a first draft: check each one against the brief, change what does not fit, and note what you changed.

Your flyer needs: a headline, the key facts (what, when, where, cost), a short body, one strong image, and a call to action ("Register at …").

Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Idea 2

Understand it

Before printing, run the proof checklist:

  1. Spelling, dates and times checked by someone else.
  2. Hierarchy: the three-second test.
  3. Everything aligned to a grid.
  4. Text contrast at least 4.5:1.
  5. Images sharp at print size, and allowed.
  6. Nothing important within 3 mm of the edge.

Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Key words

Key words

Brief
what the client needs, written down
Thumbnail
a tiny quick sketch of a layout
Proof
a final check copy before printing
Call to action
what the reader should do next
Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Read the brief and list what must be on the flyer
  2. Sketch three thumbnails, choose one
  3. Design, check, and get feedback

Need a hand? Use one template as a starting point, then change it until it fits the brief.

Done early? Design a matching square version for WhatsApp from the same content.

Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Your event flyer: link or upload the final design and your three thumbnails, and say which proof checks you did.
  • Put the flyer process in order.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.

Desktop Publishing · Week 8 · Home

At home this week
